user.title: PVAutonomy Setup
user.description:
Choose how to continue.

**Set up a new controller** — Sets up your PVAutonomy controller (currently: Edge101), the small box that connects to your inverter by cable. PVAutonomy prepares everything it needs and asks once for your Wi-Fi network. You build and install the controller's firmware yourself with the ESPHome tool — the "Local ESPHome self-build" guide walks you through every step; a USB cable is needed once. Nothing on the inverter itself is changed during setup. Once the controller is running, come back here and choose "Adopt a running controller".

**Adopt a running controller** — Registers a controller that is already running. Nothing is built, installed, or reflashed.

managed_key.title: PVAutonomy Managed Build Service
managed_key.description: Enter the Build-Key you received when activating your PVAutonomy service.

local_esphome_guide.title: Build Firmware with ESPHome
local_esphome_guide.description: On the next screens you choose your inverter model. After that you build the firmware with the ESPHome Device Builder and transfer it to the controller over USB — the "Local ESPHome self-build" guide walks you through every step. PVAutonomy prepares the credentials the build needs.

local_wifi_credentials.title: Wi-Fi for the device
local_wifi_credentials.description:
The firmware you are about to build needs to know which Wi-Fi network to join.

PVAutonomy stores what you enter here in your ESPHome `secrets.yaml` as `wifi_ssid` and `wifi_password`, so the build finds them. Entries that are already in that file are never changed, and this screen only appears for the ones that are missing.

The entry travels from this page to Home Assistant the same way every other setting you type into Home Assistant does, and is then stored in that file on this instance. It is not sent to PVAutonomy or anywhere else, and Home Assistant does not display it again.

data_description.wifi_ssid: Must be a 2.4 GHz network — the device has no 5 GHz radio. Type the name exactly as it appears, including capitals. Up to 32 characters.
data_description.wifi_password: The passphrase of that 2.4 GHz network: 8 to 63 characters, letters, digits, spaces and ordinary punctuation.

proxy.title: Self-hosted Proxy Connection
proxy.description: Advanced: configure a custom build proxy URL and credentials.

location.title: Device Location
location.description: Assign a location and device number. These identify the device in your installation.

local_yaml_confirm_existing.title: Device already exists
local_yaml_confirm_existing.description:
A device named `{device_name}` already exists in this Home Assistant, and
the settings you entered produce the same node name `{node_name}`.

Continuing means building firmware for **exactly this device** — that is
what a deliberate re-flash looks like, and it is fine if that is what you
want.

For a **new** device, go back and choose a different site or device
number. Otherwise the new firmware would carry the identity of the device
above.

data.confirm_rebuild: Yes, rebuild firmware for this existing device

target_device.title: Select Target Device
target_device.description: Choose the physical device (from Home Assistant) to bind to this configuration. Only ESPHome devices with a known MAC address are shown.

data_description.ha_device_id: Select the ESPHome device to configure. Devices that PVAutonomy already knows are marked "— re-flash". A device bound to another PVAutonomy entry cannot be adopted a second time.

confirm_relocate.title: Device Already Known
confirm_relocate.description:
This device is already registered as **{old_label}**.

Relocate to **{new_label}**?

tier_selection.title: Select Feature Level
tier_selection.description:
Choose which features to enable on the device.

**Standard** — Monitoring + APR power control (recommended for most users).
**Extended** — Battery mode, export limit, and additional battery controls. Some advanced controls remain disabled by default in Home Assistant for safety until device validation is complete.

tier_map_blocked.title: Feature Level Not Available
tier_map_blocked.description:
You selected **{requested_tier}**, but the register map check returned contradictory results for this device.

For safety, only **Standard** (Monitoring + APR) is available until the register map can be verified.

You can continue with Standard or cancel the setup.

unsafe_consent.title: Expert mode — explicit consent required
unsafe_consent.description:
These settings can cause permanent device or battery damage if used incorrectly. Examples: inverter on/off, BMS unlock, password registers.

To continue:
1) Tick the checkbox
2) Enter exactly: **{consent_phrase}**

By proceeding, you accept full responsibility for any consequences.

data.consent_checkbox: I understand the risks of these expert settings

summary.title: Confirm Device Setup

adopt_confirm.title: Adopt Running Device

adopt_name_mismatch.title: Controller Name Differs
adopt_name_mismatch.description:
The controller you selected calls itself **{node_name}** (MAC suffix `{mac_suffix}`).

From the model, location and number you entered, PVAutonomy would register it as **{device_slug}**.

If you selected the wrong controller, cancel and start again. If you are deliberately giving this controller a new location or number, continue.

progress_build.title: Building Firmware
progress_build.description:
Building firmware for **{device_name}**...

This usually takes 5–15 minutes. In some cases it may take longer. Please keep this window open and do not cancel the process.

If the connection is interrupted briefly, the build continues in the background.

progress_flash.title: Flashing Device
progress_flash.description:
Flashing firmware to **{device_name}** ({device_ip})...

Please wait, this takes about 30 seconds.

setup_complete.title: Setup Complete
setup_complete.description:
**{device_name}** — Firmware built and flashed successfully ({firmware_size} KB).

Feature level: {selected_tier} | Build-ID: `{build_id_short}`

The device is rebooting and will be online shortly.

Click **Submit** to finish.

setup_complete_cached.title: Setup Complete
setup_complete_cached.description:
**{device_name}** — Firmware loaded from cache and flashed successfully ({firmware_size} KB).

Feature level: {selected_tier} | Build-ID: `{build_id_short}`

The firmware matches the current registry for this feature level — no rebuild needed.

The device is rebooting and will be online shortly.

Click **Submit** to finish.

setup_complete_partial.title: Firmware Built
setup_complete_partial.description:
**{device_name}** — Firmware was built successfully but the device is currently offline.

The firmware is cached. You can flash it later using the **Flash** button in PVAutonomy settings.

Click **Submit** to finish.

local_yaml_ready.title: Ready to Flash
local_yaml_ready.description:
The configuration for your controller is ready — the ESPHome Device Builder already lists it as a device.

**Next steps:**

1. Open the ESPHome Device Builder. On the device, in the **⋮ menu: Validate**, then **Install** — with the controller connected by a USB data cable.
2. Once the controller is running, return to PVAutonomy and choose "Adopt a running controller".

grid_validate.description:
Projected capability state: **{projected_state}** ({reason}).
Sources: {sources}
Reduced-durability (entity-id only) mapping: {degraded}.
Submit to save this mapping.

remove.title: Remove Grid Power source
remove.description: Remove the current mapping and return Grid Power to the healthy *not configured* state. It will not be restored automatically. Current state: {capability_state}.

guide.title: Grid Power help & recovery
guide.description:
Current state: **{capability_state}** ({reason}).

- **not_configured**: healthy — Grid Power is optional.
- **not_ready** (stale): the source stopped updating — check the source device.
- **not_ready** (sign): reconfigure signed-net and confirm the sign convention.
- **not_ready** (source unresolved/missing): the mapped entity was renamed or removed — reconfigure to remap.
- **not_ready** (pair_skew): import and export update too far apart — check both meters.

Submit to return to the menu.

SHRDZM: {shrdzm_detected} detected, {shrdzm_usable} usable. If a meter is detected but not usable, it is missing channels (import 1.7.0 + export 2.7.0, or net 16.7.0) or the power metadata (device_class power, unit W).
